planting.note: Surface-sow or barely cover seed after the last frost, since light improves germination; chilling seed briefly in the freezer beforehand can improve germination rates.

directions: Asia Ip is a flat-leaf shiso selection similar in overall leaf shape and plant size to the well-known bicolor cultivar 'Britton,' but distinguished by its medium-green leaf tops and a soft pink tinge on the undersides rather than Britton's deep red-purple reverse. The uniform, full growth habit produces an abundant, continuous leaf harvest with a flavor many cooks describe as slightly stronger and more assertive than standard green shiso, carrying the familiar anise-mint-basil complex with hints of clove. Direct seed into warm soil after the last frost, thinning seedlings to allow each plant room to bush out, and pinch flowering stems to keep leaf production going through the season. The small flower spikes and immature seed heads are also edible and make an attractive, flavorful garnish alongside the leaves.
